Method of Attack: Used by North Korean hackers to steal files and send them to Google Drive storage

Backdoor malware with capabilities including stealing information from web browsers (passwords), taking screenshots, logging keystrokes, scanning local and removable drives, stealing files from connected phones, and lowering security of victim's Google account
Uses Google Drive as command and control (C2) server and to store stolen files
Establishes persistence by modifying Windows Registry
Commands delivered via Google Drive uploads; results uploaded back
Watering-hole attack using Internet Explorer exploit to deliver backdoor
Impacted Systems: Connected phones via Windows Portable Device API
Attack Vector: Watering-hole attack exploiting Internet Explorer vulnerability
Indicators of Compromise: Google Drive used as C2 server and storage
Hashes for versions 1.9 through 3.0 (86/64-bit) provided by ESET
